'''Harold Raymond Parks''' (born May 22, 1949) is an American mathematician and is a professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Oregon State University]].<ref>[http://www.math.oregonstate.edu/people/view/parks Faculty page, Oregon State University]</ref>

Parks obtained his Ph.D. in 1974 from [[Princeton University]], under the supervision of [[Frederick J. Almgren, Jr.]]<ref name="mg">{{MathGenealogy|id=17375}}</ref> In 2012, he became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-31.</ref>

He has developed and implemented a computational technique for computing parametric [[minimal surface|area minimizing surfaces]]. He derived an existence and regularity theory for a class of constrained [[Calculus of variations|variational problems]]. Parks has discovered, and characterized, a type of minimal surface with surprising properties, defined in terms of the [[Jacobi elliptic function]]s.
